fullName.note: MUST be uniquified per run, not hardcoded as literal 'Dyad Test'. new-insured-form.md's 'Duplicate-insured detection' section documents this exact case: 'Dyad Test' with this exact Insured Code (INS2516) is the specific record that was hit repeatedly, causing Create Submission to silently fail (click appears to do nothing — a toast, 'Insured Already Exists.', does flash but disappears before it's easy to catch) whenever Full Name + Mailing Address matches an existing Insured. Confirmed workaround: keep the base name for readability but append a per-run timestamp suffix (e.g. `date +"%m%d%H%M"` → 'Dyad Test 09221057'). The '{{UNIQUE_NAME:Dyad Test}}' placeholder should resolve to exactly that pattern — same base name, unique suffix — via the same per-run uniqueness approach the framework's own factories.ts already uses for applicant names (createApplicant()), not a wholly different name each time. This is also why conventions.md's 'no hardcoded... environment-specific values, use the factories' rule applies here even though Full Name isn't literally a policy/customer/claim number.

dates.note: Per explicit instruction: Proposed Effective must always be resolved to the actual run date (today), and Proposed Expiry to today + the term (12 months) — never a fixed literal date. '{{TODAY}}' / '{{TODAY+12M}}' are placeholders for a small date-resolver helper to be added to /framework/utils (e.g. dates.ts) when the create-submission page/test files are built; specs must never hardcode a literal date string for these two fields. If the app's date-picker control is awkward for direct typed input, consult alis/knowledge/pages/new-insured-form.md first for any documented date-field behavior before improvising a new interaction pattern.
